newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Orogen on track to beat forecast earnings.
newsitem.headline: Orogen on track to beat forecast earnings.

text.p: Papua New Guinea-based resources group Orogen Minerals Ltd said on Thursday that it was on track to beat its prospectus forecast earnings of 41.6 million kina (A$38.3 million) for the year to December 31, 1997.

Asked if the company would meet its prospectus forecast for calendar 1997, managing director, Charles Lepani said: "Based on our first quarter's performance, yes. We are on track to probably beat it."
Lepani, speaking to reporters after a shareholder briefing in Sydney, said first quarter earnings had been strong.

Orogen, which listed on the Australian Stock Exchange last November, posted net earnings of 16.43 million kina (A$15.46 million) in the eight months to December 31, easily beating its prospectus estimate of 12.6 million kina (A$11.86 million).
The company was formed to hold the mining and oil and gas interests of the Papua New Guinea (PNG) government which holds a 51 percent controlling interest.

Lepani said that in the past month Orogen had lifted its interest in the Lihir gold project to eight percent from 6.81 percent through on-market buying and was interest in lifting its stake further. (1 kina = A$0.92)
